message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I have $536 and a pink monopoly with 4 houses each. My opponent has only $43 and a dark blue monopoly. I am not in jail.

Player 3 is bankrupt. Player 4 has $1392 and a light blue monopoly with 4 houses each. They are in jail and have mortgaged oranges and utilities. The bank has one house left. I am reconsidering my housing lock strategy.

Hoteling one pink property would return four houses to the bank. Player 1 cannot afford a house right now with only $43. Player 4 has $1392 and might hotel their light blues if houses become available.

Player 1 can mortgage properties to raise cash for a Park Place house. I will keep my Get Out of Jail Free card for a future jail sit before the dark blues. I am on the mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue and must take a post-turn action.

All 32 houses are accounted for in the game. Player 4 holds twelve light blue houses, player 1 holds seven on dark blues, and I hold twelve pink houses.

Hotel rent on the pink properties would rise by only $200 each. Player 1 would need just one house to reach four on Park Place, which would raise that rent to $1300. A hotel there would be $1500.

Player 1 can raise enough cash to buy a house by mortgaging Kentucky, Atlantic, and Ventnor. This confirms the housing lock strategy. Player 4 already has four houses on their light blues, so they cannot build further.

Boardwalk at four houses pays $1700. My maximum liquid assets total only about $1356. I cannot afford that rent even with mortgages. Park Place at three houses pays $1100. That is barely survivable.

I cannot afford to sell houses or hotel. If Player 1 reaches four houses on Park Place, I would need to liquidate everything and remain vulnerable to the next hit.

Unmortgaging the railroads is not worthwhile. The cost exceeds the rent. Unmortgaging Tennessee is also useless without an orange monopoly.

Unmortgaging Tennessee would make it more attractive to Player 4 for completing their orange set. Player 1 will not trade away their dark blue properties. Player 4 wants Tennessee to finish their oranges, which would create another dangerous monopoly. I am weighing whether any trade could help me.

The win path is to bankrupt Player 1. If they land on a pink property and cannot pay the $750-$900 rent, they would go bankrupt and I would inherit their dark blue properties with houses still in place.

Standard Monopoly rules confirm that when a player goes bankrupt to another, buildings are sold back to the bank at half price and the proceeds go to the creditor. Mortgaged properties transfer to the new owner, who must pay 10% interest immediately or unmortgage them.

Player 1's dark blue buildings would sell for roughly $700 at half price. That plus their $43 cash is not enough to cover a pink rent. The plan is to force them onto a pink property they cannot pay and claim their empire.

Player 1 can pay a $750 pink rent by selling all seven dark blue houses and mortgaging Kentucky, Atlantic, and Ventnor. That would strip their empire and return those houses to the bank. I could then build or hotel before they rebuild.

Player 1 could pay a pink rent by selling houses and mortgaging properties. They would have roughly $213 left after paying $900 for Virginia. That is enough for one Park Place house at $200, leaving only $13. They would return to one house on Park Place rather than three.

Hotelting would release houses before Player 1 lands on my pinks. They could then build Park Place to four houses without paying me. The housing lock is therefore essential. It forces them to sell dark blue buildings when they must pay pink rent.

Selling houses would weaken my rent and free them for Player 1. I will not trade cash with anyone.

Player 4 could trade for something useful. They hold North Carolina and mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. The greens set is split between them and Player 1, so no one can complete it without a trade. Player 4 also lacks Tennessee to finish their orange set.

Rolling from Pennsylvania Avenue lands on Short Line, then Park Place, then Luxury Tax, then Boardwalk. That sequence is the danger zone. Park Place costs $1100 with three houses. Boardwalk costs $1700 with four houses.

A roll of 3 on the danger zone lands on Park Place. I can survive by selling houses and mortgage cash, but I would be left with only $36 and no buildings. A roll of 5 lands on Boardwalk, which is impossible to pay even after liquidating everything. The probability of that fatal hit is roughly 11 percent. A Chance card could also advance me directly to Boardwalk.

I cannot move before rolling. Trading away my position is impossible, and Player 1 would never accept a trade for Park Place or Boardwalk. My pink properties are my only income source, so swapping them for dark blues is unlikely to succeed. A deal with Player 4 that hurts Player 1 does not seem to help my immediate survival.

Player 1 can raise $283 by mortgaging Kentucky and Atlantic. That is enough to buy the bank's lone house. The housing lock is therefore weaker than expected.

Player 1 may have skipped building because they want to keep cash for rent survival, or because they did not notice the bank house during their last turn. They can legally add one house to Park Place to match Boardwalk at four houses, since the maximum difference is one.

Player 1 may be deliberately withholding that house to avoid raising rent to $1300. Hoteling one pink property would return four more houses to the bank, which is worse than leaving the single house there.

I will end the turn. I will post a message continuing the housing truce and warning Player 1 against building or freeing houses. Player 4 is in jail.

Player 4 can pay $50 to leave jail immediately. Staying in jail would protect them from my pinks and dark blues, but that is not a concern this turn. I am also considering a trade to acquire Pacific Avenue from Player 1 so the greens set remains incomplete.

Selling Tennessee to Player 4 would let them complete their orange set. Four houses there would pay $750 to $800 each, which is dangerous. Player 4 will not trade away their light blue monopoly for that cash. Pacific Avenue is not a useful trade target because it cannot form a monopoly.

A trade for North Carolina would give Player 4 an orange monopoly. Hoteling one property returns four houses and costs $100. That modest rent increase arms Player 1 with more cash to build on yellows. Hoteling all three pinks would return twelve houses and let both players build hotels. No trade is viable.

Player 1 cannot build on yellows because Marvin is mortgaged and they lack the $165 to unmortgage it. Their red properties are also mortgaged, so only dark blues remain buildable. If freed houses return to Park Place, Player 1 would need to hotel next, which returns four more houses and arms them with even more cash.

I will keep my public message brief and strategic. I may mention that I am not freeing houses, or stay silent to avoid revealing too much. I might also hint at Player 4's jail status to encourage them to remain there.

I want Player 4 to leave jail and land on my pinks. A $1392 light blue owner would pay me rent for free. But if they go bankrupt to Player 1, Player 1 inherits their cash and light blue monopoly. That would make them unstoppable and kill me. I will not encourage them to get out.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision for Monopoly.

I have $736 and a pink monopoly with four houses on each property. I am on MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE. I hold one Get Out of Jail Free card. I mortgaged Pennsylvania Railroad and Tennessee Avenue. The bank has one house and twelve hotels left. Opponent p1 has $43 and is in jail. They own a dark blue monopoly and some unmortgaged yellows.

p3 is bankrupt. p4 has $1,392 and owns a light blue monopoly with four houses each, plus railroads and some unmortgaged greens. The strategy is to lock in housing by not building hotels or selling houses, since the bank only has one house left and p1 could otherwise build on Park Place.

Hotel construction returns four houses to the bank, so p1 could buy them for Park Place. They have $43 cash but need $200 for a house there. Their unmortgaged properties are worth only about $110 in total, so they cannot afford it without mortgaging more.

Atlantic and Ventnor are worth $130 each, so p1 could mortgage them for cash. If I build a hotel, p1 would gain four houses to place on Park Place and potentially the yellows. Standard rents are $1,100 for three houses on Park Place, $1,300 for four, and $1,700 for four on Boardwalk. The pink properties pay $750, $750, and $900 with four houses. Selling all twelve houses would return about $600 at half price.

Liquidating all twelve houses would raise cash to about $1,336. That is enough to survive the $1,100 rent on Park Place with three houses and barely enough for four. Boardwalk with four houses still poses a risk. I landed on Mediterranean, which is mortgaged and owned by p1, so no rent was collected. The available actions are end_turn, propose_trade, unmortgage_property, build_houses_or_hotel, and sell_houses_or_hotel.

Unmortgaging the railroads is not worthwhile. The cost of $110 and $99 exceeds the mortgage value. I am now considering a trade with p4. They might want Tennessee Avenue to complete their orange monopoly.

A trade for Tennessee Avenue would let p4 complete their orange monopoly. That would create another building threat. The housing shortage still prevents them from upgrading quickly. p1 remains the main danger because they cannot afford to build a fourth house on Park Place.

P1 can mortgage Kentucky, Atlantic, and Ventnor for $370 and combine it with their $43 cash to afford the single bank house on Park Place. That would raise the rent to $1,300. They are currently in jail, but they could build before rolling if they get out. This makes the lone bank house a real threat. I am now weighing whether to hotel one of my pink properties to claim that house first.

Hotel construction is now definitively ruled out. Building a hotel on one pink property would return four houses to the bank, which p1 could then purchase. Hoteling all three properties would release twelve houses and allow both p1 and p4 to build extensively. Since each pink property already has four houses, the only available build action is hoteling.

Selling houses is also ruled out. p4's light blue properties pay $450 to $600 each with four houses, which I can afford. The pink properties are more dangerous to them.

p1 has zero jail turns and may pay to get out or try doubles. From Mediterranean, rolls of 5, 7, and 8 would hit p4's light blue properties.

The probability of landing on p4's light blue properties from Mediterranean is about 39 percent. The expected rent from those squares is roughly $500. Income Tax on roll 4 costs $200.

I will keep my Get Out of Jail Free card for when I approach the dark blues. Trading with p1 to mortgage or sell houses is unlikely to succeed, and buying Pacific from them would not help since they already own the dark blue monopoly.

I am far from the dark blues, so saving my Get Out of Jail Free card is correct. I have no action that improves my position. I will end my turn.

I am now considering trading with p1 to acquire Park Place or Boardwalk. Breaking their dark blue monopoly would be game-changing, but they are unlikely to accept my $736 cash offer since they have no cash and rely on those properties for rent.

I realized that trading Boardwalk or Park Place for cash would be unwise for p1. Even if they accepted a large cash offer, they would have to sell all buildings before trading those properties. That would destroy their dark blue monopoly and drop the rent to base levels.

Selling all buildings on Boardwalk and Park Place would return only about $500 in cash, which is too little to justify losing the dark blue rent threat. I will not propose that trade because it could signal weakness or waste one of my twenty allowed trade exchanges. I am now considering whether p4 would accept a deal to buy Tennessee Avenue to complete their orange monopoly.

Selling Tennessee Avenue to p4 would give them an orange monopoly. They could place one house on an orange property, but the bank only has one house left, so the immediate threat is small. Orange properties pay $550 to $600 for three houses and $950 to $1,000 for hotels, making them dangerous long-term.

I rejected the idea of selling Tennessee Avenue to p4 because it would give them an orange monopoly. Acquiring North Carolina or New York from p4 is useless since I have no other greens, and splitting the orange set is impossible. A railroad monopoly is also not worth the cost. I will end my turn without proposing trades.

I will keep my public message short and consistent. I passed GO and now have $736, but I still will not build hotels. p1 is in jail with only $43, so they cannot pay the $50 bail to get out; they must stay and roll for doubles or mortgage a property to cover it. While in jail, p1 cannot move toward collecting rent from my pink properties.

p1 is stuck in jail without a Get Out of Jail Free card, so they will attempt doubles for the next three turns. I will end my turn and keep my public message brief. I updated the cash math: selling all twelve houses would raise my balance to $1,336, which covers the $1,100 rent on Park Place with three houses but barely covers four houses.
